title: Solution structure of domain 1.1 of the σA factor from Bacillus subtilis is preformed for binding to the RNA polymerase core.
experiment: 15N R1, R2 (CPMG pulse spacing 0.83 ms), steady-state [1H]-15N NOE (ssNOE), and longitudinal/transverse cross-correlated relaxation (Gamma_z, Gamma_x) at 600, 850, and 950 MHz (d'Auvergne model-free analysis in relax)
construct_or_mutation: B. subtilis sigmaA domain 1.1 (residues Ala1-Asp71 plus XhoI linker Leu72-Glu73 and C-terminal His6 tag; 9.4 kDa, 15N- or 13C,15N-labeled)
other_conditions: 0.6 mM 15N-labeled or 0.8 mM 13C,15N-labeled monomeric sample; tumbling: prolate spheroid global correlation time (1/6Diso) = 6.13 ns at 25 °C, D||/Dperp = 2.23; decreased S2 in HII-HIII loop (E42-E44) and beta-sheets (V28-T30, E61-I63); significant Rex contributions in helix I (F12-R26, especially terminal regions), C-terminal part of helix II (Y31-F41), and beta-sheet II (E61-I63) and vicinity; 仅图示: per-residue S2, Sf2, tau_e, tau_s, and Rex values are plotted only in Figure 2 (deposited in BMRB 27011)
residues_author: A1-T11 (N-terminus), F12-R26 (helix I; L19, E21), V28-T30 (beta-sheet I; V28), Y31-F41 (helix II; E33, R37), E42-E44 (HII-HIII loop), S45-E57 (helix III; S45, D46), Q58-D71 (C-terminus, including beta-sheet II E61-I63)
timescale: tau_s = ~1 ns (terminal regions; L19 SD = 1.6 ns, V28 SD = 1.8 ns); residues exceeding 100 ps plot range in Fig. 2B: E21 = 1.2 ± 1.2 ns; E33 = 0.8 ± 0.7 ns; R37 = 0.7 ± 0.5 ns; D46 = 0.9 ± 0.2 ns; S45 SD = 334 ps (d'Auvergne extended Lipari-Szabo model-free fit in relax)
related_structures: 5MWW (B. subtilis apo sigma1.1 ground-state solution NMR structure); 4LK1, 4YLN (E. coli RNAP-sigma70 crystal structures)
author_claim: Multi-field 15N spin relaxation shows complex multi-timescale internal dynamics in B. subtilis sigma1.1, with reduced S2 in the HII-HIII loop and beta-sheet, ~1 ns terminal motions, and widespread Rex terms in helix I, late helix II, and beta-sheet II.
anchor: plotted range, are not shown: Glu21, 1.2 ⫾ 1.2 ns; Glu33, 0.8 ⫾ 0.7 ns; Arg37,
locator: Results, 15N relaxation, p. 11611-11612 and Fig. 2, p. 11613 (仅图示 for full per-residue profiles); conditions: Experimental procedures, Sample preparation and NMR measurements, p. 11615-11616
caveat_note: Relaxation rates and model-free order parameters were explicitly deposited in BMRB 27011 (p. 11616). However, pH and buffer composition are not reported anywhere in the paper or supplement (whereas the BMRB 27011 card specifies pH 6.6, 20 mM phosphate buffer, 10 mM NaCl, 6 mM sodium azide, 0.6 mM [U-100% 15N] sigma1.1 at 298.2 K [= 25 °C], sequence length 73 = Ala1-Asp71 + Leu72-Glu73 preceding the His6 tag). Internal text/figure discrepancies: Results text (p. 11612) refers to Fig. 2B for tau_s and Fig. 2C for Rex, whereas in Fig. 2 panel B is tau_e, panel C is tau_s, and panel D is Rex; also Fig. 2B caption ('B, effective correlation time tau_e') prints 'Standard deviations of tau_s of Ser45 was 334 ps' before listing off-scale values for Glu21, Glu33, Arg37, and Asp46.

title: Solution structure of domain 1.1 of the σA factor from Bacillus subtilis is preformed for binding to the RNA polymerase core.
experiment: 15N CPMG relaxation dispersion (CPMG frequency 111 to 2000 Hz) at 600, 850, and 950 MHz (relax autoanalysis)
construct_or_mutation: B. subtilis sigmaA domain 1.1 (residues Ala1-Asp71 plus XhoI linker Leu72-Glu73 and C-terminal His6 tag; 9.4 kDa, 15N- or 13C,15N-labeled)
other_conditions: 0.6 mM 15N-labeled or 0.8 mM 13C,15N-labeled sample; regime (authors): slow conformational exchange / slow exchange (ms-us time scale); pB standard deviations for E21 and D46 = 0.087 and 0.089, respectively; authors speculate the minor state may resemble the perpendicular-HI fold of T. maritima sigma1.1; 仅图示: per-residue kex, pB, and delta_omega plotted in Figure 3
residues_author: E21, D46; F12-R26 (end of helix I), Y31-F41 (helix II), E61-I63 (beta-sheet II)
timescale: kex = ~3,500 Hz; delta_omega(15N) = 2 to 6 ppm (two-state CPMG dispersion model in relax)
population: minor conformational state pB = 1.5% (pB SD: E21 = 0.087, D46 = 0.089)
related_structures: 5MWW (B. subtilis apo sigma1.1 ground-state solution NMR structure); 4LK1, 4YLN (E. coli RNAP-sigma70 crystal structures)
author_claim: 15N CPMG relaxation dispersion at 600, 850, and 950 MHz reveals a two-state conformational exchange at kex ~ 3,500 Hz with a 1.5% minor state showing 2-6 ppm 15N chemical shift differences concentrated at the end of helix I, helix II, and beta-sheet II.
anchor: Hz and with the minor state being populated by 1.5% (Fig. 3).
locator: Results, 15N relaxation, p. 11612 and Fig. 3, p. 11613 (仅图示 for per-residue kex, pB, delta_omega); Discussion, p. 11615; conditions: Experimental procedures, NMR measurements, p. 11615-11616
caveat_note: Experimental procedures (p. 11615) states all NMR experiments were performed at 25 °C using either a 0.8 mM 13C,15N-labeled or 0.6 mM 15N-labeled sample without specifying which sample was used for CPMG dispersion and without reporting pH or buffer composition (BMRB 27011 card specifies 0.6 mM [U-100% 15N] sigma1.1, pH 6.6, 20 mM phosphate buffer, 10 mM NaCl, 6 mM sodium azide at 298.2 K). Atomic structure of the 1.5% minor state is unresolved; similarity to T. maritima sigma1.1 is explicitly presented as an untested hypothesis.

title: Solution structure of domain 1.1 of the σA factor from Bacillus subtilis is preformed for binding to the RNA polymerase core.
experiment: Comparison and Molsoft docking of B. subtilis apo sigma1.1 solution NMR structure (5MWW; NOEs, 3JHNHA, and 86 RDCs in 5% polyacrylamide gel) against E. coli RNAP-bound sigma1.1 (4LK1, 4YLN)
buffer: 5% polyacrylamide gel for aligned RDC measurement (base buffer not reported)
ligand_or_partner: apo in solution (5MWW) modeled into B. subtilis RNAP core homology model based on E. coli RNAP holoenzyme (4LK1)
construct_or_mutation: B. subtilis sigmaA domain 1.1 (residues Ala1-Asp71 plus XhoI linker Leu72-Glu73 and C-terminal His6 tag; 9.4 kDa, 13C,15N- or 15N-labeled)
other_conditions: 5MWW ensemble (20 structures, structured core residues 10-63 backbone RMSD = 0.38 ± 0.10 Å; 1886 NOEs, 21 3JHNHA, 86 helical RDCs from 1D(HNH), 1D(CaC'), 1D(NC'), 2D(HNC); chemical shifts in BMRB 34089); all-antiparallel packing of helices HI-HIII anchored by F12 nestled among M38, F41, and I43 plus beta-sheet V28-T30 / E61-I63; unstructured N-terminus (A1-T11) and C-terminal linker (Q58-D71, except E61-I63)
residues_author: A1-T11, F12-R26 (helix I; F12, R26), G27-T30 (HI-HII loop; beta-strand V28-T30), Y31-F41 (helix II; E36, M38, F41), E42-E44 (HII-HIII loop; E42, I43, E44), S45-E57 (helix III; D46, E50, F54, E57), Q58-D71 / E73 (C-terminus; beta-strand E61-I63, E65, E67, E68, E70, D71, E73)
related_structures: 5MWW (B. subtilis apo sigma1.1 ground-state solution NMR structure); 4LK1, 4YLN (E. coli RNAP-sigma70 crystal structures)
author_claim: Free B. subtilis sigma1.1 in solution (5MWW) adopts a compact all-antiparallel three-helix fold resembling RNAP-bound E. coli sigma1.1 (4LK1) and fits smoothly into the RNAP downstream DNA channel with minimal conformational rearrangement.
anchor: Comparison of 3D structures of ␴1.1 from B. subtilis, E. coli, and T. maritima with the N-terminal domain of the RNAP ␦ subunit from B. subtilis.
locator: Results, Structure of sigma1.1 and Position of sigma1.1 within the DNA-binding channel of RNAP, p. 11611-11613, Table 1, and Fig. 1, 4, 5; Discussion, p. 11614-11615; Experimental procedures, p. 11615-11616; supp_PMC5512058_10.1074_M117.784074_jbc.M117.784074-1.pdf, Fig. S1 and Fig. S2
caveat_note: Structure determination used 0.8 mM 13C,15N-labeled (and 5% polyacrylamide gel aligned RDC) samples deposited in PDB 5MWW / BMRB 34089 rather than the isotropic 0.6 mM 15N relaxation sample in BMRB 27011, and no experimental B. subtilis RNAP-sigma1.1 complex structure was determined (RNAP placement is an in silico Molsoft alignment on E. coli template 4LK1). Although no large free-to-bound fold rearrangement is required for the major state, CPMG dispersion (r2) shows free B. subtilis sigma1.1 still exchanges with a 1.5% minor conformation in solution.

title: Solution structure of domain 1.1 of the σA factor from Bacillus subtilis is preformed for binding to the RNA polymerase core.
experiment: Structural comparison and Molsoft RNAP-channel docking of Thermotoga maritima free sigma1.1 solution structure against E. coli RNAP-bound sigma1.1 (4LK1) and B. subtilis sigma1.1 (5MWW)
ligand_or_partner: free solution structure vs modeled RNAP DNA-binding channel complex
construct_or_mutation: Thermotoga maritima primary sigma factor domain 1.1 (homolog)
other_conditions: T. maritima sigma1.1 has an unstructured non-conserved N-terminus (~1-30) and a long helix HI packed perpendicularly to HII and HIII (resembling B. subtilis RNAP delta subunit helices HIa+HIb, HII, HIII), causing steric clash with the RNAP downstream DNA channel unless HI rearranges
related_structures: 5MWW (B. subtilis apo sigma1.1); 4LK1, 4YLN (E. coli RNAP-sigma70 crystal structures)
author_claim: Structural alignment into the RNAP core shows that helix I of T. maritima free sigma1.1 does not fit into the downstream DNA-binding channel and must undergo a conformational rearrangement to bind RNAP.
anchor: This leads to the all-anti-parallel packing of the B. subtilis and E. coli σ1.1 structures that markedly differs from that of T. maritima σ1.1
locator: Abstract, p. 11610; Discussion, sigma1.1 structure comparisons and sigma1.1 interactions with RNAP, p. 11614-11615 and Fig. 5; supp_PMC5512058_10.1074_M117.784074_jbc.M117.784074-1.pdf, Fig. S1 and Fig. S2
caveat_note: In silico structural comparison of previously published T. maritima sigma1.1 NMR structure (Ref. 15; PDB code not printed in paper) docked onto the RNAP core template rather than direct experimental measurement on B. subtilis SigA (BMRB 27011).
